question: Does contemporaneous local vegetation green-up improve held-out-year radar spring-passage date reconstruction beyond site-specific calendar baseline, linear year trend and average spring temperature?

source.radar_origins: NOAA weather surveillance radar (bird assemblage), not eBird
source.author_2015_2025_prior_art: The original paper already found interannual temperature dominates greenup as a passage predictor; not a new discovery.

units.inference: unique radar station x year; independent year is time-transfer unit, not 833 independent species/animals
units.y: spring_q50 = DOY when 50% of season passage observed at station
units.x_t: spring_mean_temp = author-derived spring interval average temperature, measured retrospectively not necessarily before departure
units.x_g: mean_greenup = author-derived mean MODIS greenup DOY for site-year; can be known only after greenup occurs
units.calendar: linear year trend plus each radar's own baseline, fit only on training years

model.baseline: spring_q50 ~ station fixed intercepts + centered numeric year + spring_mean_temp
model.augmented: spring_q50 ~ station fixed intercepts + centered numeric year + spring_mean_temp + mean_greenup
model.training: whole-year leave-one-year-out, 16 folds if support passes, shared complete cases
model.inference: mean of per-year heldout MSE difference baseline minus augmented, equal year weight
model.secondary: fraction of years with positive gain; descriptive full-data partial greenup coefficient with no claim of causal cue
model.only_one_quantile: spring_q50 only; do not search q10/q90 when q50 is null

uncertainty.method: paired year-level nonparametric bootstrap of 16 precomputed year-specific heldout MSE differences; fixed seed
uncertainty.positive_decision: CI lower bound > 0, and at least 10 of the 16 individual year folds show positive gain; otherwise NO_ROBUST_GAIN

ecological_limits: Retroactive full-season climate and greenup predictors are not actual cues available to birds at decision time
This is assemblage radar, not individual migration decisions, fitness, recourse or partner synchrony
Positive association does not prove green-wave tracking, information learning or ecological fitness
No claims of new independent original data collection or of novel greenup-temperature relationship (already published)
Do not equate NDVI greenup with biomass or actual prey without independent validation
Do not combine this input with any eBird data, including eBird-derived products
release_state: Only original-source hashes, aggregate support, computed model summary and code are saved. Raw station names and data rows are NOT committed. Keep draft separate from main/frozen manuscripts.
